title: TOOLS-GITIGNORE-001: replace the blanket /tools/ ignore with declared intent
intent: A blanket /tools/ ignore silently drops NEW files added to tracked tool packages. Tests still pass because the file is on disk, git status still looks clean because the file is ignored, and the PR ships incomplete. Already-tracked files behave normally throughout, which is what makes it hard to notice. Replace the blanket rule with an explicit allowlist of deliberately tracked families, and pin it with a regression witness.
behavior_change: No runtime behaviour changes; .gitignore and one new test file. Every file currently tracked under tools/ remains tracked and un-ignored (verified against all 19). New files added to a declared tool package are now visible to git instead of silently ignored. New UNDECLARED loose files at the tools/ root remain ignored by design -- adding a tool family means declaring it.

diff_articulation.what_changed: `/tools/` becomes `/tools/*` plus explicit `!` re-admissions for the four tracked packages (codegen, grounding_agent, grounding_agent/adapters, agent_program) and the nine tracked loose root files, followed by `/tools/**/__pycache__/` to re-ignore bytecode. New test file asks `git check-ignore` directly for each case.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The origin of the rule was established rather than assumed: `git blame` puts it at 8261fc87 (2025-12-14), whose message is 'Anchor patterns to prevent blocking nested app code -- fixes 136+ files in services/api/app/ being incorrectly ignored'. That commit NARROWED a broader `tools/` pattern to `/tools/`; it did not decide to ignore repository tooling. A pickaxe over .gitignore history returns no other commit touching the pattern, so no commit anywhere states an intent to ignore tools/. The rule is inherited, not chosen, which is why documenting the `git add -f` workaround would have preserved a defect rather than fixed one.

commands_run: inventory: git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- tools/ -> 19 tracked files across 3 package dirs and 9 loose root files (agent_program adds 3 more when PR #340 merges)
origin: git blame .gitignore -> 8261fc87 2025-12-14; git log -S'tools/' -- .gitignore -> that commit only
no regression: every one of the 19 tracked files checked with git check-ignore -> none ignored

THE WITNESS CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THE FIX ITSELF. The first draft's `!/tools/<pkg>/**` rules are LATER than the global `__pycache__/` rule (line 20), and gitignore's last-match-wins meant un-ignoring a package also un-ignored its bytecode. test_generated_content_under_tools_stays_ignored failed; `/tools/**/__pycache__/` added.
check-ignore is queried via subprocess and rc>1 is raised rather than folded into 'not ignored', so a broken invocation cannot read as a passing test

files.intent: Replace the inherited blanket /tools/ ignore with `/tools/*` plus declared re-admissions, and re-ignore generated bytecode inside them.
files.behavior_change: new files in declared tool packages are visible to git; undeclared loose root files stay ignored by design

files.intent: Regression witness. Probes a path that does not exist on disk, because the failure mode is about files added LATER -- testing an existing tracked file would pass even under the blanket rule, since tracking survives .gitignore.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: The one low item is a finding recorded but deliberately NOT resolved here: a developer working checkout carries 11 untracked, ignored files at the tools/ root -- README.md, _audit_orphan_router_candidates.py, _audit_unregistered_routers.py, compare_golden_cli.py, compare_report_cli.py, compare_report_lib.py, compare_run_cli.py, generate_bundle_issue_templates.py, golden_compare_lib.py, wp002_import_census.py, and standalone/. They remain ignored under the repaired rule, because the repair re-admits named families rather than the whole directory. Whether any of them is intended repository tooling or personal scratch is unknown and is the owner's call, not this increment's. Recorded so the question is answerable rather than invisible.
